newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Senate summons Olivetti's Caio for hearing.
newsitem.headline: Italian Senate summons Olivetti's Caio for hearing.

text.p: The industry committee in the Italian upper house of parliament (Senate) said on Tuesday it had summoned Olivetti managing director Francesco Caio to appear at a regular hearing on Thursday morning.

A committee spokeswoman said the hearing was a normal procedure after the group's announcement last week that it made a 440.2 billion lire ($291.3 million) loss for the first half of this year and following the resignation of chairman Carlo De Benedetti.
The Caio hearing will be followed by one for the metal and engineering unions, who on Monday called an eight hour strike for September 27 to back their wage claim.

Olivetti shares fell 20 percent on the Milan bourse after a two-day suspension on Thursday and Friday, and hit a fresh record low at 575 lire on Tuesday morning. It was trading at 580 lire by 1410 GMT.
Olivetti said in a statement on Tuesday that Caio would meet equity analysts in Milan on September 16 and would then travel to London for further meetings with analysts.
